messages.subject: Google Code Shutting Down
messages.body_plain:
From: http://google-opensource.blogspot.co.uk/2015/03/farewell-to-google-code.html

"Beginning today, we have disabled new project creation on Google Code. We will be shutting down the service about 10 months from now on January 25th, 2016. Below, we provide links to migration tools designed to help you move your projects off of Google Code. We will also make ourselves available over the next three months to those projects that need help migrating from Google Code to other hosts.”

What is the thought here, move it, or let RPostgreSQL die in favor of the other R connectors?

Neil

--

messages.subject: Re: Google Code Shutting Down
messages.body_plain:
Hadley Wickham was working on 
https://github.com/rstats-db/RPostgres,  it seems very active with commits over the last few months, but I have not been following the status.

There are several issues with RPostgreSQL, moving the repository, maintaining compatibility with R-DBI changes, and then there are a number of open issues that would normally have been responded to by Tomoaki, but he has been silent the last few months.

I probably have time to move the repository, but if we don’t have a maintainer for *nix and Windows, then it may be pointless.

Neil

messages.subject: Re: dbListTables doen't list views. dbListViews?
messages.body_plain:
> On Mar 26, 2015, at 5:04 AM, Domenico Giusti <dncgst-Re5JQEeQqe8AvxtiuMwx3w at public.gmane.org> wrote:
> 
> Hi all,
> 
> I wonder how to list views, if possible. Does it exist a dbListViews?
> 
> Thanks a lot,
> 

dbListViews  does not exist, try the following SQL

	select schema name, viewname from pg_catalog.pg_views;

or 

	select schemaname, viewname from pg_catalog.pg_views
	where schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')
	order by schema name, viewname;

Neil

--

messages.body_plain:
Dear Neil,

it works, thank you!

## Submits a statement
rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "SELECT viewname from pg_catalog.pg_views where 
viewowner = 'user'")
## Fetch all elements from the result set
fetch(rs,n=-1)

Best,
